correctness.rationale: The displayed coupled Sylvester system has exact X=e₁e₁ᵀ and operator gaps −1,−3,1,−1, so its minimum singular value is one. Independent Haar u,v yield s=u₂²,t=v₂² independent arcsine. Reduced x=−u₁v₁/[2(s−t)−1] and Z=√((1−s)(1−t))/|2(s−t)−1|. Conditional on t<1/2, the r=√(1−s) tail interval has exact width √(1−t)/(2R), yielding RPr(Z>R)→(1/π²)∫₀^{1/2}dt/√(t(t+1/2))=2asinh(1)/π². The t>1/2 part is O(R⁻³); dominated convergence and layer cake prove p-moment finiteness iff p<1 for Z and error. Fresh symbolic/minimal-gap/integral checks support analysis, not simulation of infinite moments.
